newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 8.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 8.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The Australian government decided late on Monday to only partially ease rules stopping mergers between Australia's four largest banks and two largest life insurance groups, The Australian Financial Review reported. Treasurer Peter Costello would retain a discretionary veto over any merger or acquisition, the newspaper said. All major banks and the ACCC have argued against the Treasurer retaining the right to reject mergers, saying the ACCC alone should have that power.

A parcel of 23.9 million or about three percent of Fairfax shares were traded late in Monday trade. The trade was seen as Merrill Lynch passing on to institutional investors part of the 4.9 percent stake it bought from Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc last month. Merrill Lynch is expected to pass the rest on at some later stage.
The Australian government has decided not to ban Australis Media Ltd's pay television pornography channel, Night Moves, a spokesman for Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Tuesday.
Coal group QCT Resources Ltd said late on Monday it expected a lower profit for the year to June 30, 1997 due to the higher Australian dollar and lower coal prices in the fourth quarter.

The Financial Review said a U.S. District Court judge had cleared the way for a class action to be mounted over Pacific Dunlops's Telecontronics heart pacemaker leads, a move which would shock Pacific Dunlop.
